description: The shared fix-in-place loops the review and security-stage agents run, against the per-language criteria and security guides they are often confused with.

queries.query: Do a repo-scale review of this Go module and fix the problems in place, verifying the build after each edit.
Review the whole Python package and fix issues directly. Edit in place, don't just report.
Run a fix-in-place review over src/ in this TypeScript project, with a severity-rated report at the end.
Review this Rust workspace and apply the fixes yourself, reverting anything that breaks cargo test.
Readonly review of the Node.js service: report the findings by severity and change nothing.
Review and fix this module in place. Security is out of scope; just correctness and design.
Review the nodejs codebase and fix bugs in place, with a final report that lists every change.
Run a scoped security audit of the auth package and fix the vulnerabilities in place, reverting any fix that breaks the tests.
Audit internal/api for injection bugs and fix them in place, verifying the build after each edit.
Do a readonly security audit of the Python upload handlers and give me findings in the standard severity format.
Run a fix-in-place audit of our Express app for path traversal and SSRF.
Audit the Go service for resource issues (temp files, weak crypto, TLS config) and fix what you find.
Scoped security audit of cmd/ only, in edit mode. Wind down cleanly when you hit the budget.
Find and fix the SQL injection risks in this Python repo, then run the tests.
What are the most common Go concurrency bugs?
What should a Python code review checklist include?
List the OWASP Top 10.
Review this one-line change: `timeout = 30` became `timeout = 60`.
Write tests for the auth package.
Explain what SSRF is.
